text: RESOLVED: local JVM process serving a browser UI -- the RStudio Server / Jupyter / TensorBoard pattern. Backend (JVM) does parsing, detection, estimation and storage; frontend is Scala.js over HTTP + WebSocket on localhost; domain types and codecs are shared across the wire. Distributed as a jpackage/jlink bundle. Rationale: decided by data governance more than technology. Eye-tracking files are large (1000 Hz binocular for an hour is 100MB+ of ASC) and are human-subjects data, so a hosted app means uploading participant gaze off-site -- an IRB and liability problem. A native desktop app is install friction on managed institutional machines plus per-OS signing and update infrastructure. A Tauri-style hybrid would run the heavy parsing as Scala.js in a webview, making the biggest files the slowest case. CONSEQUENCE: Scala Native remains unnecessary post-1.0, and the Scala.js investment is confirmed load-bearing (APP-19).
